entities.summary:
Qvarqvare I Jaqeli was a Georgian prince (mtavari) and ruler of Samtskhe during 1334-1361.

He was the son of Prince Japhar II Jaqeli and succeeded him to the throne in 1334.

Qvarqvare I Jaqeli played a crucial role in the consolidation of the Georgian Kingdom of Samtskhe, which was a major power in the region during the 14th century.

He strengthened the kingdom's economy and military, and expanded its borders through strategic alliances and military campaigns.

Despite his significant contributions, Qvarqvare I Jaqeli's reign was marked by internal conflicts and power struggles with neighboring kingdoms.

He died in 1361, leaving behind a legacy of military victories and territorial gains that shaped the future of the Georgian Kingdom.

One of the most striking aspects of Qvarqvare I Jaqeli's reign was the significant role he played in the Black Death's impact on the Georgian Kingdom, with estimates suggesting that up to 50% of the kingdom's population was killed by the pandemic.

As he was remembered by later generations as a great leader, Qvarqvare I Jaqeli's legacy continues to be studied by historians today.

In the annals of Georgian history, he is remembered as a hero who brought peace and prosperity to the kingdom during a time of great turmoil.
